candidate.answerReason: The left triangle gives angle 1=70°, so angle 2=110°. The remaining two angles in the right triangle are equal and sum to 70°, giving angle 4=35°.

methods.label: Use the two triangle angle sums
methods.explanation:
The left triangle has two known angles, so its angle sum determines \(\angle1\):
\[
\angle1=180^\circ-40^\circ-70^\circ=70^\circ.
\]
The given relation \(\angle1+\angle2=180^\circ\) then gives \(\angle2=110^\circ\).

In the right-hand triangle, the other two angles must sum to
\[
\angle3+\angle4=180^\circ-110^\circ=70^\circ.
\]
Since \(\angle3=\angle4\), each is half of \(70^\circ\). Thus \(\angle4=\boxed{35^\circ}\), choice \(\boxed{\text{D}}\).
